messages.subject: the shiny function landscape
parts:
The "shiny function landscape" table below is helping me understand a few things that had me royally confused.
It is constructed by searching the shiny package object names for strings "^reactive" etcetera
(with a few tweaks).
Some observations: 
  • outputs and inputs are nonintersecting except for "text".
  • two "Input$" functions do not have "Input" in the name (indicated by parentheses)
  • most "^reactive" functions are now deprecated (dep), replaced by "^render" functions;  some are not. 
  • generally, "^render" and "Output$" functions are matched, but with 3 exceptions.
  • update functions exist for "Input$" functions except "file".
You can change an output object easily; include a reactive expression.
Not so easy with input objects.
However, the update functions provide a way to change an input object.
through "sending a message" via session$sendInputMessage().
This is handled by the javascript input bindings for "receiveMessage" 
in the shiny package's shiny.js file.
 
Aside: I'm really interested in using jstree objects in shiny.
There are two implementations currently (shinysky and shinyTree).
They are both promising,
but neither seems to follow the function naming convention closely.
In  shinysky there's an Input called jstree().
In  shinyTree there's an Output called shinyTree(), and a render called renderTree().

I desperately need my tree to be both interactive and reactive
(for example, select a node and click a Remove button, & that changes the tree's data model and updates display of the tree).
To do that seems to require an input function and matching update function, and matching receiveMessage in javascript.
So far it looks like that approach will work. All advice and critique welcome!
